item.title: San Francisco A Day in Pleasanton
item.description: Pleasanton hides a picture book Main Street in the Tri-Valley, where a drive through dairy has scooped soft serve since before the freeways arrived. Eight
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in Pleasanton

Pleasanton hides a picture book Main Street in the Tri-Valley, where a drive through dairy has scooped soft serve since before the freeways arrived. Eight Pleasanton stops.

Gay Nineties Pizza Co — 288 Main St, Pleasanton. A beloved old school parlor slinging award winning pies for decades. Get a pitcher and a pepperoni.

Meadowlark Dairy — 57 W Neal St, Pleasanton. A drive through dairy famous for soft serve, busy even on cold days. Roll up for a cone.

Baci Bistro and Bar — 500 Main St, Pleasanton. A downtown Italian room with a retro glow and a lively bar. Book a booth.

Towne Center Books — 555 Main St, Pleasanton. An independent bookstore that anchors the downtown, author events and staff picks. Ask for a rec.

Museum on Main — 603 Main St, Pleasanton. A local history museum in an old storefront telling the valley's story. Catch a walking tour.

Firehouse Arts Center — 4444 Railroad Ave, Pleasanton. A restored firehouse turned theater and gallery. Check the marquee.

The Rose Hotel — 807 Main St, Pleasanton. A boutique hotel on Main Street with old world rooms and a downtown perch. Stay the weekend.

Alameda County Fairgrounds — 4501 Pleasanton Ave, Pleasanton. The historic fairgrounds and horse track that hosts the summer county fair. Time a visit to the fair.

Eight in Pleasanton: Gay Nineties Pizza, Meadowlark Dairy, Baci Bistro, Towne Center Books, Museum on Main, the Firehouse, the Rose Hotel, and the Fairgrounds. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Rooftop Bars
item.description: The Bay Area saves its best skyline views for its rooftops, from a Market Street penthouse bar to a Berkeley beer garden over Shattuck. Eight Bay Area roof
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Rooftop Bars

The Bay Area saves its best skyline views for its rooftops, from a Market Street penthouse bar to a Berkeley beer garden over Shattuck. Eight Bay Area rooftop bars.

Charmaine's — 1100 Market St, SF. A penthouse rooftop at the Proper Hotel with firepits and a sweeping city view. Get there for sunset.

620 Jones — 620 Jones St, SF. A big heated terrace bar off Union Square, planted and lively year round. Come for happy hour.

Kaiyo Rooftop — 701 3rd St, SF. A plant draped Nikkei rooftop near Oracle Park with Peruvian Japanese small plates. Order a pisco.

Cavaña — 100 Channel St, SF. A Mission Bay rooftop at the LUMA Hotel with firepits and DJ nights near the ballpark. Grab a firepit.

Rise Over Run — 950 Market St, SF. A greenhouse style rooftop atop The LINE hotel that shrugs off the fog. Sit in the atrium.

Dirty Habit — 12 4th St, SF. A fifth floor terrace lounge at Hotel Zelos with craft cocktails and small plates. Try the oysters.

The View Lounge — 780 Mission St, SF. A top floor sky lounge in the Marriott Marquis with floor to ceiling skyline windows. Go up at dusk.

Comal — 2020 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A downtown Berkeley rooftop beer garden over a modern Mexican kitchen. Start with a margarita.

Eight Bay Area rooftops: Charmaine's, 620 Jones, Kaiyo, Cavaña, Rise Over Run, Dirty Habit, the View Lounge, and Comal. Which view first?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Polk Street
item.description: Swan Oyster Depot has served raw oysters from the same marble counter on Polk Street since 1912, cash only, no reservations, a line out the door every day.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Polk Street

Swan Oyster Depot has served raw oysters from the same marble counter on Polk Street since 1912, cash only, no reservations, a line out the door every day. Eight Polk Street stops.

Swan Oyster Depot — 1517 Polk St, SF. The 1912 seafood counter locals line up for, oysters and cracked crab on ice. Get the combo and a beer.

Bob's Donuts — 1621 Polk St, SF. A 24 hour donut institution famous for a giant apple fritter. Try the fritter warm.

Cheese Plus — 2001 Polk St, SF. A corner cheese shop and deli building serious grilled cheese and picnic boards. Order the classic grilled cheese.

Amélie — 1754 Polk St, SF. A candlelit French wine bar with flights and a lively happy hour. Do a flight.

Nick's Crispy Tacos — 1500 Broadway at Polk, SF. A rowdy taco spot and bar, fish tacos done Nick's Way. Order them Nick's Way.

The Bell Tower — 1900 Polk St, SF. A classic corner pub with big windows and a solid brunch. Grab a window table.

Leopold's — 2400 Polk St, SF. An Austrian tavern with pretzels, schnitzel, and boots of beer. Split a boot.

House of Prime Rib — 1906 Van Ness Ave, SF. The 1949 prime rib palace a block off Polk, carved tableside from silver carts. Book ahead for the City cut.

Eight on Polk Street: Swan Oyster Depot, Bob's Donuts, Cheese Plus, Amélie, Nick's Crispy Tacos, the Bell Tower, Leopold's, and House of Prime Rib. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Potrero Hill
item.description: Potrero Hill catches more sun than almost any corner of foggy San Francisco, and its 18th Street spine is a village of sourdough pizza and hillside cafes m
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Potrero Hill

Potrero Hill catches more sun than almost any corner of foggy San Francisco, and its 18th Street spine is a village of sourdough pizza and hillside cafes most of the city drives past. Eight Potrero Hill stops.

Goat Hill Pizza — 300 Connecticut St, SF. A Potrero classic making sourdough crust pizza since 1975, Monday all you can eat. Come for the sourdough.

Plow — 1299 18th St, SF. The brunch spot with a line, famous for lemon ricotta pancakes and the potatoes. Get there early.

Farley's — 1315 18th St, SF. A beloved indie coffeehouse and community hub since 1989. Linger with a latte.

Chez Maman — 1401 18th St, SF. A tiny French bistro with mussels, crepes, and a cult burger. Squeeze in at the counter.

Aperto — 1434 18th St, SF. A neighborhood Italian room with handmade pasta and regulars at every table. Ask the daily pasta.

Christopher's Books — 1400 18th St, SF. A cozy corner indie bookstore anchoring the strip. Leave with a staff pick.

Klein's Deli — 501 Connecticut St, SF. A corner deli and market stacking big sandwiches for the hill. Grab one to go.

The Good Life Grocery — 1524 20th St, SF. A Potrero independent grocery since 1974, a neighborhood cornerstone. Pick up picnic supplies.

Eight on Potrero Hill: Goat Hill Pizza, Plow, Farley's, Chez Maman, Aperto, Christopher's Books, Klein's Deli, and the Good Life Grocery. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Outer Richmond
item.description: Out where San Francisco runs into the ocean fog, the Outer Richmond hides a sleeper strip of Balboa Street wine bars, a 1953 Russian bakery, and old school
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Outer Richmond

Out where San Francisco runs into the ocean fog, the Outer Richmond hides a sleeper strip of Balboa Street wine bars, a 1953 Russian bakery, and old school burger joints most of the city never reaches. Eight Outer Richmond stops.

Simple Pleasures Cafe — 3434 Balboa St, SF. A bohemian coffeehouse and SF Legacy Business since 1978, live music some nights. Sink into a couch.

Balboa Theatre — 3630 Balboa St, SF. A nearly century old twin cinema showing new releases and old indies. Catch a matinee.

Pizzetta 211 — 211 23rd Ave, SF. A tiny beloved wood fired pizzeria a block off Balboa, a weekly changing menu. Go early, it is small.

Ton Kiang — 5821 Geary Blvd, SF. A Cantonese and Hakka favorite with weekend cart dim sum. Come for the dumplings.

Cinderella Bakery — 436 Balboa St, SF. A Russian bakery and cafe since 1953, piroshki and black bread. Get a piroshki.

Kabuto — 5121 Geary Blvd, SF. A revered tiny omakase sushi bar in the Richmond. Sit at the bar.

Pearl 6101 — 6101 California St, SF. A sunny neighborhood restaurant with a great oyster happy hour near the Presidio edge. Do the oyster hour.

Bill's Place — 2315 Clement St, SF. A 1959 burger joint with a garden patio and named burgers. Order a namesake burger.

Eight in the Outer Richmond: Simple Pleasures, the Balboa Theatre, Pizzetta 211, Ton Kiang, Cinderella Bakery, Kabuto, Pearl 6101, and Bill's Place. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Jackson Square and the Classics
item.description: Tadich Grill has been open since 1849, the oldest restaurant in California, and it anchors a downtown pocket of Gold Rush saloons and white tablecloth room
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Jackson Square and the Classics

Tadich Grill has been open since 1849, the oldest restaurant in California, and it anchors a downtown pocket of Gold Rush saloons and white tablecloth rooms that outlasted everything around them. Eight downtown classics.

Tadich Grill — 240 California St, SF. California's oldest restaurant, since 1849, cioppino and sand dabs at a wood counter. Order the cioppino.

Sam's Grill — 374 Bush St, SF. An 1867 seafood house of curtained booths and old world service. Get a curtained booth.

The Old Ship Saloon — 298 Pacific Ave, SF. A saloon on the site of a beached Gold Rush ship, pouring since 1851. Toast the ship below the floor.

Kokkari Estiatorio — 200 Jackson St, SF. A fireside Greek institution in Jackson Square, lamb and meze. Get the lamb chops.

Cotogna — 490 Pacific Ave, SF. A rustic Italian favorite with wood fired pasta and pizza. Book ahead for the pasta.

Bix — 56 Gold St, SF. A supper club down a hidden alley with martinis and live jazz. Order a martini upstairs.

Comstock Saloon — 155 Columbus Ave, SF. A restored Barbary Coast saloon with classic cocktails and a ragtime piano. Sit at the antique bar.

William Stout Architectural Books — 804 Montgomery St, SF. A landmark design and art bookstore in Jackson Square since 1974. Browse the art shelves.

Eight downtown classics: Tadich Grill, Sam's Grill, the Old Ship Saloon, Kokkari, Cotogna, Bix, Comstock Saloon, and William Stout Books. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Presidio Heights
item.description: Sacramento Street through Presidio Heights is where San Francisco locals shop when they want quiet boutiques and a Michelin kitchen instead of a crowd, lea
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Presidio Heights

Sacramento Street through Presidio Heights is where San Francisco locals shop when they want quiet boutiques and a Michelin kitchen instead of a crowd, leafy blocks of storefronts near the Presidio gate. Eight Sacramento Street stops.

Spruce — 3640 Sacramento St, SF. A Michelin starred neighborhood restaurant with a famous burger at the bar. Get the Spruce burger.

Books Inc — 3515 California St, SF. The Laurel Village outpost of the Bay Area's oldest bookseller, since 1851. Catch an author night.

Cal-Mart — 3585 California St, SF. A beloved independent grocery with a great butcher and deli counter. Grab lunch at the deli.

Bryan's — 3445 California St, SF. A high end market and butcher, prime meat and prepared foods. Pick up a roast.

Osteria — 3277 Sacramento St, SF. A snug family trattoria with handmade pasta. Split the pasta.

Sue Fisher King — 3067 Sacramento St, SF. A refined home and gift boutique, linens and tableware. Find a hostess gift.

Ella's — 500 Presidio Ave, SF. A corner brunch institution famous for sticky buns and chicken hash. Come for the sticky buns.

b — Patisserie. 2821 California St, SF. A celebrated French patisserie near Presidio Heights, the kouign amann is the move. Get the kouign amann.

Eight in Presidio Heights: Spruce, Books Inc, Cal-Mart, Bryan's, Osteria, Sue Fisher King, Ella's, and b. Patisserie. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Union Square
item.description: Union Square is where San Francisco's cable cars turn around by hand on a giant wooden turntable, ringed by grand hotels, department stores, and a martini
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Union Square

Union Square is where San Francisco's cable cars turn around by hand on a giant wooden turntable, ringed by grand hotels, department stores, and a martini bar straight out of The Maltese Falcon. Eight Union Square stops.

Powell Street Cable Car Turnaround — Powell St at Market, SF. The downtown terminus where crews spin the cars by hand. Watch them turn a car.

John's Grill — 63 Ellis St, SF. A 1908 chophouse out of The Maltese Falcon, martinis and steaks. Order the Sam Spade lamb chops.

Westin St — Francis. 335 Powell St, SF. The 1904 grand hotel on the square with a famous magic clock in the lobby. Meet under the clock.

Britex Fabrics — 117 Post St, SF. A four floor fabric emporium and city institution since 1952. Get lost on the trim floor.

Maiden Lane — Maiden Lane, SF. A pedestrian shopping lane with the city's only Frank Lloyd Wright building. Walk the Wright spiral.

Union Square Park — 333 Post St, SF. The palm ringed heart of downtown under the Dewey victory column. Sit and people watch.

The Rotunda at Neiman Marcus — 150 Stockton St, SF. Lunch under a 1909 stained glass dome, popovers and tea. Come for a popover.

Chinatown Dragon Gate — Grant Ave at Bush St, SF. The dragon crowned gateway a block off the square into Chinatown. Walk through into Chinatown.

Eight at Union Square: the cable car turnaround, John's Grill, the Westin St Francis, Britex Fabrics, Maiden Lane, Union Square Park, the Neiman Marcus Rotunda, and the Chinatown Gate. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco A Day On Burlingame Avenue
item.description: Burlingame Avenue is the Peninsula's small town main street, a walkable stretch of pizza ovens and candy counters just south of San Francisco, with the old
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day On Burlingame Avenue

Burlingame Avenue is the Peninsula's small town main street, a walkable stretch of pizza ovens and candy counters just south of San Francisco, with the old railway depot anchoring the far end. Eight Burlingame Avenue stops.

Il Fornaio — 327 Lorton Ave, Burlingame. A bustling Italian bakery and trattoria off the avenue, wood fired everything. Start with the bread basket.

Crepevine — 1310 Burlingame Ave, Burlingame. A NorCal creperie for sweet and savory crepes and big breakfasts. Get a savory crepe.

Preston's Candy and Ice Cream — 1213 Burlingame Ave, Burlingame. A 1946 candy and ice cream parlor making chocolates in house. Get a hand dipped cone.

Copenhagen Bakery — 1216 Burlingame Ave, Burlingame. A Danish bakery and cafe with marzipan cakes and open faced sandwiches. Take home a kringle.

Steelhead Brewing — 333 California Dr, Burlingame. A longtime brewpub by the depot, house lagers and burgers. Grab a house lager.

Burlingame Railroad Station — 290 California Dr, Burlingame. The 1894 depot, among the oldest still in use in California. See the tile roof.

Books Inc — 1375 Burlingame Ave, Burlingame. The avenue's independent bookstore branch, story times and staff picks. Grab a beach read.

Village Host Pizza and Grill — 1451 Burlingame Ave, Burlingame. A casual local pizza and salad spot on the avenue. Split a pie.

Eight on Burlingame Avenue: Il Fornaio, Crepevine, Preston's, Copenhagen Bakery, Steelhead Brewing, the 1894 depot, Books Inc, and Village Host Pizza. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Pizza
item.description: The Bay Area's most decorated pizzaiolo has won the world championship in Naples, but the best slice around might be a Berkeley collective with a line down
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Pizza

The Bay Area's most decorated pizzaiolo has won the world championship in Naples, but the best slice around might be a Berkeley collective with a line down the sidewalk and a single pie a day. Eight Bay Area pizzerias.

Tony's Pizza Napoletana — 1570 Stockton St, SF. The North Beach temple from a world champion pizzaiolo, many styles from many ovens. Order the Margherita, limited daily.

Cheese Board Pizza — 1512 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. The Berkeley collective with one vegetarian pie a day, a jazz combo, and a line down the block. Get whatever is on.

Zachary's Chicago Pizza — 5801 College Ave, Oakland. The Rockridge deep dish institution, stuffed crust worth the wait. Get the stuffed spinach and mushroom.

Pizzeria Delfina — 3611 18th St, SF. The Mission Neapolitan spot behind Delfina, blistered thin crust. Get the Napoletana.

Del Popolo — 855 Bush St, SF. A wood fired standout that started as a shipping container oven, now a glass walled room. Order the Margherita.

Flour and Water Pizza Shop — 702 Valencia St, SF. A slice shop from the Flour and Water team, thick square Sicilian and pepperoni. Grab a square.

Little Star Pizza — 400 Valencia St, SF. A San Francisco deep dish favorite with a cornmeal crust. Get the Classic deep dish.

Emilia's Pizzeria — 2995 Shattuck Ave, Berkeley. A tiny Berkeley shop serving New York style by preorder, revered. Preorder a whole pie.

Eight Bay Area pizzerias: Tony's, the Cheese Board, Zachary's, Pizzeria Delfina, Del Popolo, Flour and Water, Little Star, and Emilia's. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Cow Hollow and Union Street
item.description: Balboa Cafe has poured drinks on the same Cow Hollow corner since 1913, the anchor of a Union Street stretch of brunch spots and boutiques where cows once
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Cow Hollow and Union Street

Balboa Cafe has poured drinks on the same Cow Hollow corner since 1913, the anchor of a Union Street stretch of brunch spots and boutiques where cows once grazed the marsh. Eight Union Street stops.

Rose's Cafe — 2298 Union St, SF. The sunny corner brunch spot with mimosas and a sidewalk full of regulars. Get a window table.

Perry's — 1944 Union St, SF. A Union Street institution for burgers, martinis, and streetside people watching. Order the burger.

Balboa Cafe — 3199 Fillmore St, SF. A saloon since 1913, dark wood and a famous namesake burger. Belly up to the bar.

West Coast Wine and Cheese — 2165 Union St, SF. A cozy wine bar pouring California by the glass with boards to match. Ask for a flight.

Blue Barn — 2105 Union St, SF. A bright spot for big made to order salads and sandwiches. Build a chopped salad.

The Brixton — 2140 Union St, SF. A lively bar and grill packed on game nights. Come for happy hour.

Roam Artisan Burgers — 1785 Union St, SF. Grass fed burgers built your way with house sauces. Add the sweet potato fries.

Brazen Head — 3166 Buchanan St, SF. A hidden pub with no sign, candlelit and cash only, a Cow Hollow secret. Find the unmarked door.

Eight on Union Street: Rose's Cafe, Perry's, Balboa Cafe, West Coast Wine and Cheese, Blue Barn, the Brixton, Roam, and the Brazen Head. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Lower Haight
item.description: Toronado has poured a legendary beer list on Lower Haight since 1987, the loud anchor of a compact bar strip locals call the triangle of alcohol. Eight Low
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Lower Haight

Toronado has poured a legendary beer list on Lower Haight since 1987, the loud anchor of a compact bar strip locals call the triangle of alcohol. Eight Lower Haight stops.

Toronado — 547 Haight St, SF. A legendary beer bar since 1987 with a chalkboard of rare taps. Order something Belgian.

Mad Dog in the Fog — 530 Haight St, SF. A British pub for footy, fry ups, and pints. Catch a match.

Molotov's — 582 Haight St, SF. A punky dive with a pool table and no pretense. Stay late.

Noc Noc — 557 Haight St, SF. A cave like bar of steampunk booths and cheap beer and sake. Grab a booth.

Kate's Kitchen — 471 Haight St, SF. A beloved brunch counter with big biscuits and hush puppies. Come hungry, cash helps.

Uva Enoteca — 568 Haight St, SF. A warm Italian wine bar with small plates and by the glass pours. Split the burrata.

The Little Chihuahua — 581 Haight St, SF. A local favorite for sustainable tacos and plantain burritos. Get the plantain burrito.

Danny Coyle's — 668 Haight St, SF. An Irish pub with a patio, trivia, and live music. Post up on the patio.

Eight in Lower Haight: Toronado, Mad Dog in the Fog, Molotov's, Noc Noc, Kate's Kitchen, Uva Enoteca, the Little Chihuahua, and Danny Coyle's. Where do you start?

item.title: SF's Mission Bay
item.description: Mission Bay went from rail yards and warehouses to San Francisco's newest neighborhood in a decade, built around the Warriors arena, a food truck park, and
item.content:encoded:
SF's Mission Bay

Mission Bay went from rail yards and warehouses to San Francisco's newest neighborhood in a decade, built around the Warriors arena, a food truck park, and a creek where houseboats still bob. Eight Mission Bay stops.

Chase Center — 1 Warriors Way, SF. The Warriors arena and its plaza, concerts and games on the bay. Catch an event at Thrive City.

Gott's Roadside — 151 Warriors Way, SF. A modern roadside burger and shake stand at Thrive City. Get a burger and a shake.

Spark Social SF — 601 Mission Bay Blvd N, SF. A rotating food truck park with fire pits and a beer garden. Graze the trucks.

The Ramp — 855 Terry Francois Blvd, SF. A ramshackle bayfront restaurant with a patio and weekend live music. Sit on the water.

Mission Creek Park — Channel St at 4th, SF. A little waterway lined with houseboats and kayakers. Watch the houseboats.

Philz Coffee — 165 Berry St, SF. The Mint Mojito crowd's morning stop by the creek. Order a Mint Mojito iced.

UCSF Mission Bay — 1825 4th St, SF. The research campus green with public art and a quiet quad. Walk the Koret Quad.

Crane Cove Park — 18 Georgia St, SF. A waterfront park with a little beach and the old shipyard cranes. Bring a blanket.

Eight in Mission Bay: Chase Center, Gott's, Spark Social, the Ramp, Mission Creek Park, Philz, UCSF, and Crane Cove Park. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Hayes Valley
item.description: Hayes Valley traded a double deck freeway for a leafy boutique district after the 1989 quake brought it down, and now its blocks pack Michelin kitchens, ma
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Hayes Valley

Hayes Valley traded a double deck freeway for a leafy boutique district after the 1989 quake brought it down, and now its blocks pack Michelin kitchens, macarons, and nitrogen ice cream. Eight Hayes Valley stops.

Rich Table — 199 Gough St, SF. A Michelin star kitchen famous for sardine chips and porcini doughnuts. Start with the doughnuts.

Absinthe Brasserie — 398 Hayes St, SF. A French brasserie and cocktail bar, the neighborhood's grand old room. Order a classic cocktail.

Souvla — 517 Hayes St, SF. A fast fine Greek spot known for spit roasted lamb and frozen Greek yogurt. Get the lamb salad.

Hayes Street Grill — 320 Hayes St, SF. A seafood classic by the opera house since 1979. Order the fish of the day.

Birba — 458 Grove St, SF. A tiny wine bar with a heated patio and Italian pours. Grab a patio seat.

Smitten Ice Cream — 432 Octavia St, SF. Ice cream frozen to order with liquid nitrogen in a little kiosk. Watch it freeze.

Chantal Guillon — 437 Hayes St, SF. A macaron atelier with rows of pastel shells. Build a box of six.

Anina — 482 Hayes St, SF. A playful cocktail bar with frozen drinks and a patio. Do a frozen negroni.

Eight in Hayes Valley: Rich Table, Absinthe, Souvla, Hayes Street Grill, Birba, Smitten, Chantal Guillon, and Anina. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco A Day in Los Gatos
item.description: Los Gatos tucks a Michelin Greek room, a cult bread bakery, and a 1927 movie palace into a walkable downtown at the foot of the Santa Cruz Mountains. Eight
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in Los Gatos

Los Gatos tucks a Michelin Greek room, a cult bread bakery, and a 1927 movie palace into a walkable downtown at the foot of the Santa Cruz Mountains. Eight Los Gatos stops.

Dio Deka — 210 E Main St, Los Gatos. A Michelin Greek room with a fireplace at Hotel Los Gatos. Book the lamb chops.

Manresa Bread — 276 N Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos. The cult bakery spun off from the famed restaurant, kouign amann and country loaves. Grab a pastry.

Los Gatos Coffee Roasting — 101 W Main St, Los Gatos. A downtown roaster and cafe on the corner for decades. Sit outside with a latte.

The Bywater — 532 N Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos. Chef David Kinch's New Orleans kitchen, gumbo and po'boys with a raw bar. Order the gumbo.

Forbes Mill Steakhouse — 206 N Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos. A downtown steakhouse named for the town's old flour mill. Get a martini and a ribeye.

Icing on the Cake — 50 N Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos. A bakery famous for its towering layer cakes. Take home a slice.

Testarossa Winery — 300A College Ave, Los Gatos. A tasting room in an old stone winery, Pinot and Chardonnay. Taste a flight.

Los Gatos Theatre — 41 N Santa Cruz Ave, Los Gatos. A 1927 movie palace with a neon marquee still lighting Main Street. Catch a show.

Eight in Los Gatos: Dio Deka, Manresa Bread, Los Gatos Coffee Roasting, the Bywater, Forbes Mill, Icing on the Cake, Testarossa, and the theatre. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco Mountain View's Castro Street
item.description: Mountain View's Castro Street is Silicon Valley's real downtown, a walkable strip where engineers line up for tapas, wood fired pizza, and a Michelin tasti
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Mountain View's Castro Street

Mountain View's Castro Street is Silicon Valley's real downtown, a walkable strip where engineers line up for tapas, wood fired pizza, and a Michelin tasting menu hidden off the main drag. Eight Castro Street stops.

Cascal — 400 Castro St, Mountain View. A lively tapas bar of Spanish and Latin plates and sangria. Share a table of tapas.

Scratch — 401 Castro St, Mountain View. A from scratch American kitchen with a patio and brunch. Come for weekend brunch.

Doppio Zero — 160 Castro St, Mountain View. A Neapolitan pizzeria with a certified wood fired oven. Order a Margherita.

Red Rock Coffee — 201 Castro St, Mountain View. A two story community cafe with open mics and laptops. Grab an upstairs seat.

Books Inc — 317 Castro St, Mountain View. The downtown independent bookstore with author nights. Leave with a staff pick.

Casa Lupe — 253 Castro St, Mountain View. A family Mexican spot with margaritas and combo plates. Get the enchiladas.

Chez TJ — 938 Villa St, Mountain View. A Michelin tasting menu tucked in a Victorian off the strip. Book the tasting.

Steins Beer Garden — 895 Villa St, Mountain View. A big beer garden with house brews and long tables. Post up outside.

Eight on Castro Street: Cascal, Scratch, Doppio Zero, Red Rock Coffee, Books Inc, Casa Lupe, Chez TJ, and Steins. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Ramen
item.description: The Bay Area's ramen obsession runs from a Japantown counter with an hour wait to a Sonoma shop making its own noodles from local grain. Eight Bay Area ram
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Ramen

The Bay Area's ramen obsession runs from a Japantown counter with an hour wait to a Sonoma shop making its own noodles from local grain. Eight Bay Area ramen bowls.

Marufuku Ramen — 1581 Webster St, SF. A Japantown favorite with silky Hakata tonkotsu and a long wait. Get the tonkotsu.

Hinodeya — 1737 Buchanan St, SF. A Japantown shop known for a lighter dashi based broth. Try the dashi ramen.

Iza Ramen — 237 Fillmore St, SF. A Lower Haight bowl shop that grew from a pop up. Order the spicy miso.

Ramen Shop — 5812 College Ave, Oakland. A Rockridge spot from Chez Panisse alums with seasonal bowls. Get whatever is seasonal.

Ramen Nagi — 541 Bryant St, Palo Alto. A build your own Butao bowl with rich broth, always a line. Customize the Butao King.

Ramen Dojo — 805 S B St, San Mateo. A tiny San Mateo counter with a cult following and a wait. Go early or wait.

Orenchi Ramen — 3540 Homestead Rd, Santa Clara. A South Bay original famous for its tonkotsu. Line up before it opens.

Ramen Gaijin — 6948 Sebastopol Ave, Sebastopol. A Sonoma County shop making noodles from local grain. Try the shoyu.

Eight Bay Area ramen bowls: Marufuku, Hinodeya, Iza, Ramen Shop, Ramen Nagi, Ramen Dojo, Orenchi, and Ramen Gaijin. Which bowl first?

item.title: Bay Area Bakeries and Croissants
item.description: The Bay Area might bake the best croissant in America, and the reigning champions run from a corner shop in the foggy Richmond to a wood oven in Petaluma.
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Bakeries and Croissants

The Bay Area might bake the best croissant in America, and the reigning champions run from a corner shop in the foggy Richmond to a wood oven in Petaluma. Eight Bay Area bakeries.

Arsicault Bakery — 397 Arguello Blvd, SF. A Richmond corner shop whose almond croissant won national best new bakery. Get the almond croissant.

Tartine Bakery — 600 Guerrero St, SF. The Mission institution with a morning bun worth the line. Get a morning bun.

Jane the Bakery — 1881 Geary Blvd, SF. A big airy bakery and cafe with house breads and pastries. Grab a loaf and a coffee.

Neighbor Bakehouse — 2343 3rd St, SF. A Dogpatch bakery famous for its everything croissant. Get the everything croissant.

Fournée Bakery — 2912 Domingo Ave, Berkeley. A tiny Berkeley shop by the Claremont with a killer kouign amann. Go early, it sells out.

Starter Bakery — 3418 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. An Oakland bakery known for its kouign amann and canelés. Try the kouign amann.

Model Bakery — 1357 Main St, St Helena. A Napa Valley bakery whose English muffin became famous. Get the English muffin.

Della Fattoria — 141 Petaluma Blvd N, Petaluma. A wood oven bakery and cafe in downtown Petaluma. Grab a slab of focaccia.

Eight Bay Area bakeries: Arsicault, Tartine, Jane, Neighbor Bakehouse, Fournée, Starter, Model Bakery, and Della Fattoria. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Russian Hill
item.description: Swensen's has scooped ice cream at the top of the Hyde Street cable car line since 1948, the sweet anchor of a Russian Hill worth the climb for crooked str
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Russian Hill

Swensen's has scooped ice cream at the top of the Hyde Street cable car line since 1948, the sweet anchor of a Russian Hill worth the climb for crooked streets and hidden stairways. Eight Russian Hill stops.

Swensen's Ice Cream — 1999 Hyde St, SF. The original parlor since 1948 at Hyde and Union, small batch scoops. Get a hot fudge sundae.

Frascati — 1901 Hyde St, SF. A cozy Italian bistro right on the cable car line. Book a window table.

Za Pizza — 1919 Hyde St, SF. A neighborhood slice shop with thin crust pies and a chill vibe. Grab two slices.

Pesce — 2227 Polk St, SF. A Venetian seafood spot built for grazing small plates. Order a spread of cicchetti.

Helmand Palace — 2424 Van Ness Ave, SF. A longtime Afghan restaurant famous for its pumpkin kaddo. Start with the kaddo.

Lombard Street — Lombard St at Hyde, SF. The famously crooked block of switchbacks and flower beds. Walk down the brick curves.

Ina Coolbrith Park — Vallejo St at Taylor, SF. A steep terraced hillside park with a knockout bay view. Climb up at golden hour.

Macondray Lane — Macondray Ln, SF. A hidden wooden staircase lane, the model for the Barbary Lane of Tales of the City. Find the secret stairs.

Eight in Russian Hill: Swensen's, Frascati, Za Pizza, Pesce, Helmand Palace, Lombard Street, Ina Coolbrith Park, and Macondray Lane. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Noe Valley
item.description: Noe Valley is San Francisco's sunny stroller valley, a 24th Street of bakeries and bistros tucked just below the fog line where the J Church rattles past.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Noe Valley

Noe Valley is San Francisco's sunny stroller valley, a 24th Street of bakeries and bistros tucked just below the fog line where the J Church rattles past. Eight Noe Valley stops.

Firefly — 4288 24th St, SF. A cozy contemporary American spot that has owned date night for decades. Book a table.

Noe Valley Bakery — 4073 24th St, SF. The neighborhood bakery for morning buns and celebration cakes. Grab a morning bun.

La Ciccia — 291 30th St, SF. A beloved Sardinian restaurant famous for spicy octopus and bottarga. Order the octopus.

La Boulangerie de San Francisco — 3898 24th St, SF. A French bakery cafe for kouign amann and quiche. Get a kouign amann.

Barney's Gourmet Hamburgers — 4162 24th St, SF. A local burger institution with a hidden back patio. Take a booth out back.

Chloe's Cafe — 1399 Church St, SF. A tiny brunch corner with a weekend line for the pancakes. Come early.

Hamlet — 1199 Church St, SF. A neighborhood wine bar with cheese and charcuterie. Split a board.

Toast Eatery — 1748 Church St, SF. An all day breakfast spot with big plates by the streetcar. Get the eggs benedict.

Eight in Noe Valley: Firefly, Noe Valley Bakery, La Ciccia, La Boulangerie, Barney's, Chloe's Cafe, Hamlet, and Toast. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco A Day in Petaluma
item.description: Petaluma kept the small town main street Hollywood keeps filming, a walkable riverfront of a wood fired bakery, a beer garden, and a 1911 music hall about
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in Petaluma

Petaluma kept the small town main street Hollywood keeps filming, a walkable riverfront of a wood fired bakery, a beer garden, and a 1911 music hall about an hour north of the city. Eight Petaluma stops.

Central Market — 42 Petaluma Blvd N, Petaluma. A farm to table New American room with a wood oven and a nearby farm. Book ahead.

Della Fattoria Downtown Cafe — 143 Petaluma Blvd N, Petaluma. The famous wood fired bakery and cafe for bread and breakfast. Get the egg on a bun.

Seared — 170 Petaluma Blvd N, Petaluma. A live fire steakhouse with lobster mac and happy hour. Order a steak.

Petaluma Pie Company — 125 Petaluma Blvd N, Petaluma. A little shop for sweet and savory hand pies. Grab a savory pie.

Brewsters Beer Garden — 229 Water St N, Petaluma. A riverside beer garden with fire pits and long tables. Grab a picnic table.

Lala's Creamery — 134 Petaluma Blvd N, Petaluma. A downtown ice cream parlor with homemade scoops. Get a double.

Copperfield's Books — 140 Kentucky St, Petaluma. The North Bay indie bookstore's Petaluma shop. Browse the stacks.

Mystic Theatre — 21 Petaluma Blvd N, Petaluma. A historic 1911 music hall still booking live shows. Catch a set.

Eight in Petaluma: Central Market, Della Fattoria, Seared, Petaluma Pie, Brewsters, Lala's Creamery, Copperfield's Books, and the Mystic Theatre. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Oyster Bars and Seafood
item.description: The Bay Area slurps oysters at a marble counter that has barely changed since 1912 and cracks crab on a Tomales Bay dock, some of the best seafood on the c
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Oyster Bars and Seafood

The Bay Area slurps oysters at a marble counter that has barely changed since 1912 and cracks crab on a Tomales Bay dock, some of the best seafood on the coast. Eight Bay Area oyster and seafood spots.

Swan Oyster Depot — 1517 Polk St, SF. The 1912 marble counter for oysters and cracked crab, cash only. Get the combo.

Hog Island Oyster Co — 1 Ferry Building, SF. The Ferry Building raw bar pulling Tomales Bay oysters with a water view. Do a dozen.

Anchor Oyster Bar — 579 Castro St, SF. A Castro seafood counter since 1977, cioppino and oysters. Get the cioppino.

Sotto Mare — 552 Green St, SF. A North Beach seafood joint famous for its crab cioppino. Order the cioppino.

Woodhouse Fish Co — 2073 Market St, SF. A New England style fish shack for lobster rolls and oysters. Get a lobster roll.

Scoma's — 1965 Al Scoma Way, SF. A Fisherman's Wharf seafood institution since 1965, pier to plate. Order the Dungeness.

Alamar Kitchen — 100 Grand Ave, Oakland. An Oakland seafood boil spot for shrimp and crab by the bag. Get a boil bag.

Nick's Cove — 23240 Highway 1, Marshall. A Tomales Bay oyster roadhouse on the water. Slurp oysters on the dock.

Eight for seafood: Swan Oyster Depot, Hog Island, Anchor Oyster Bar, Sotto Mare, Woodhouse, Scoma's, Alamar, and Nick's Cove. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Ethiopian
item.description: The Bay Area's best Ethiopian food clusters along a single stretch of Oakland's Telegraph Avenue, where you scoop spicy stews with spongy injera and no for
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Ethiopian

The Bay Area's best Ethiopian food clusters along a single stretch of Oakland's Telegraph Avenue, where you scoop spicy stews with spongy injera and no fork in sight. Eight Bay Area Ethiopian tables.

Cafe Colucci — 6427 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A family run room since 1991 with old school stews and a combo platter. Get the veggie combo.

Cafe Romanat — 462 21st St, Oakland. A warm favorite for spicy tibs and honey wine. Order the tibs.

Enssaro — 357 Grand Ave, Oakland. A Grand Avenue spot for a big injera combo. Share a platter.

Asmara — 5020 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A longtime Eritrean and Ethiopian kitchen. Try the zilzil tibs.

Barcote — 6430 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A Temescal favorite for kitfo and combos. Get the kitfo.

New Eritrea Restaurant and Bar — 907 Irving St, SF. An Inner Sunset stalwart for injera and stews. Order the vegetarian combo.

Zeni Ethiopian — 1320 Saratoga Ave, San Jose. A South Bay spot with spicy red lentils and gored gored. Get the gored gored.

Walia Ethiopian — 2208 Business Cir, San Jose. A San Jose favorite for tibs and injera. Share the combo.

Eight for injera: Cafe Colucci, Cafe Romanat, Enssaro, Asmara, Barcote, New Eritrea, Zeni, and Walia. Where do you start?

item.description: The Bay Area's barbecue runs deep, from an Oakland institution smoking ribs by Jack London Square to a Divisadero backyard pit with a cult burger, Texas br
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Barbecue

The Bay Area's barbecue runs deep, from an Oakland institution smoking ribs by Jack London Square to a Divisadero backyard pit with a cult burger, Texas brisket to Memphis ribs across the whole bay. Eight Bay Area barbecue joints.

Roderick's Barbecue — 2708 98th Ave, Oakland. A deep East Oakland pit turning out Texas style brisket and hot links, go before it sells out. Get the brisket early.

Smokin Woods BBQ — 4307 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. An Oakland smokehouse loved for ribs and burnt ends. Order the burnt ends.

Everett and Jones Barbeque — 126 Broadway, Oakland. A Jack London Square institution with a family recipe sauce. Get the links.

Phat Matt's BBQ — 4622 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A neighborhood spot for tri tip and brisket plates. Order the tri tip.

KC's BBQ — 2613 San Pablo Ave, Berkeley. A Berkeley classic smoking ribs for decades. Get a rib plate.

4505 Burgers and BBQ — 705 Divisadero St, SF. A Divisadero backyard smoker for brisket and a cult burger. Try the brisket.

Memphis Minnie's — 576 Haight St, SF. A Lower Haight barbecue joint for pulled pork and ribs. Order the pulled pork.

Smoking Pig BBQ — 1144 N 4th St, San Jose. A South Bay smokehouse for brisket and links. Get the combo plate.

Eight for smoke: Roderick's, Smokin Woods, Everett and Jones, Phat Matt's, KC's, 4505, Memphis Minnie's, and Smoking Pig. Where do you start?

item.description: The Bay Area chases Vietnamese food from a clear northern pho in the Financial District to San Jose banh mi lines that run out the door, a scene as deep as
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Vietnamese

The Bay Area chases Vietnamese food from a clear northern pho in the Financial District to San Jose banh mi lines that run out the door, a scene as deep as it gets. Eight Bay Area Vietnamese stops.

Turtle Tower — 220 California St, SF. The FiDi shop for clear northern style pho ga since 1999. Order the pho ga.

Bodega Bistro — 607 Larkin St, SF. A Little Saigon room for Hanoi street food and cha ca. Get the cha ca.

Yummy Yummy — 1015 Irving St, SF. An Inner Sunset favorite for bun and pho, always packed. Get the bun bo Hue.

Tay Ho — 344 12th St, Oakland. An Oakland spot known for banh cuon and com tam. Order the banh cuon.

Binh Minh Quan — 8045 International Blvd, Oakland. An International Boulevard pho house with a big menu. Get a bowl of pho.

Vung Tau — 535 E Santa Clara St, San Jose. A San Jose institution for a wide Vietnamese spread. Try the shaking beef.

Huong Lan — 1655 Tully Rd, San Jose. The banh mi and deli line that stretches out the door. Grab a banh mi.

Rose International Market — 1060 Castro St, Mountain View. A market and banh mi counter with a cult following. Order a banh mi.

Eight for Vietnamese: Turtle Tower, Bodega Bistro, Yummy Yummy, Tay Ho, Binh Minh Quan, Vung Tau, Huong Lan, and Rose Market. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco A Day in Downtown Napa
item.description: Downtown Napa turned its riverfront into a food hall, a Michelin bistro row, and a 1937 theater, proof the valley's best table might be in town instead of
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in Downtown Napa

Downtown Napa turned its riverfront into a food hall, a Michelin bistro row, and a 1937 theater, proof the valley's best table might be in town instead of out on the vineyards. Eight downtown Napa stops.

Oxbow Public Market — 610 1st St, Napa. A riverside food hall of oyster bars, tacos, and coffee under one roof. Graze the stalls.

Oenotri — 1425 1st St, Napa. A downtown Italian spot with house salumi and a daily changing menu. Get the pasta.

Grace's Table — 1400 2nd St, Napa. A cheerful Bib Gourmand bistro for all day comfort food. Order the cast iron cornbread.

Angele Restaurant and Bar — 540 Main St, Napa. A French brasserie in an 1890s ship chandlery on the river. Sit on the riverfront patio.

Compline — 1300 1st St, Napa. A wine bar, shop, and restaurant from a master sommelier. Ask for a pour flight.

Cadet Wine and Beer Bar — 930 Franklin St, Napa. A lively downtown bar pouring off the beaten path bottles. Let them pick.

Napa Valley Wine Train — 1275 McKinstry St, Napa. A vintage rail dining trip up the valley from downtown. Book the lunch run.

Uptown Theatre — 1350 3rd St, Napa. A restored 1937 art deco theater booking live music. Catch a show.

Eight in downtown Napa: Oxbow Public Market, Oenotri, Grace's Table, Angele, Compline, Cadet, the Wine Train, and the Uptown Theatre. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Speakeasies and Hidden Bars
item.description: San Francisco keeps its best cocktails behind unmarked doors and moving bookcases, a password speakeasy scene that started in a Tenderloin apothecary. Eigh
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Speakeasies and Hidden Bars

San Francisco keeps its best cocktails behind unmarked doors and moving bookcases, a password speakeasy scene that started in a Tenderloin apothecary. Eight SF hidden bars.

Bourbon and Branch — 501 Jones St, SF. The original SF speakeasy behind an unmarked door, password required. Reserve the Library room.

Wilson and Wilson — 505 Jones St, SF. A detective themed speakeasy hidden inside Bourbon and Branch. Book the tiny room.

Local Edition — 691 Market St, SF. A subterranean newspaper themed bar with nightly live jazz. Go for the jazz set.

Pagan Idol — 375 Bush St, SF. A downtown tiki den with volcano cocktails and hut booths. Order a volcano to share.

The Devil's Acre — 256 Columbus Ave, SF. An apothecary themed bar mixing 1880s recipes in North Beach. Try an old remedy.

Smuggler's Cove — 650 Gough St, SF. A three story pirate tiki temple with hundreds of rums. Get the Dead Reckoning.

Trick Dog — 3010 20th St, SF. A Mission cocktail den with a menu that reinvents itself every few months. Order off the theme.

Rickhouse — 246 Kearny St, SF. A two story bourbon bar built from reclaimed barrel wood. Get a punch bowl for the table.

Eight SF hidden bars: Bourbon and Branch, Wilson and Wilson, Local Edition, Pagan Idol, the Devil's Acre, Smuggler's Cove, Trick Dog, and Rickhouse. Where do you start?

item.title: San Francisco SF's Live Music Venues
item.description: San Francisco's oldest bar has hosted live blues since 1861, the low end of a music scene that runs up to a chandeliered rock hall where the Dead cut their
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Live Music Venues

San Francisco's oldest bar has hosted live blues since 1861, the low end of a music scene that runs up to a chandeliered rock hall where the Dead cut their teeth. Eight SF music venues.

The Fillmore — 1805 Geary Blvd, SF. The legendary rock hall with chandeliers and free posters at the door. Grab an apple upstairs.

Great American Music Hall — 859 O'Farrell St, SF. An ornate 1907 hall with balconies and great sound. Get a spot on the balcony rail.

Bimbo's 365 Club — 1025 Columbus Ave, SF. A 1931 supper club with red curtains and old glamour. Dress up a little.

The Chapel — 777 Valencia St, SF. A former mortuary chapel with a 40 foot arched ceiling. Stand center floor.

The Warfield — 982 Market St, SF. A 1922 vaudeville theater turned mid size rock room. Book the balcony.

The Independent — 628 Divisadero St, SF. A beloved midsize club for breakout acts. Get there early, it is standing room.

Cafe du Nord — 2174 Market St, SF. A dark basement club below an old speakeasy. Catch a late set.

The Saloon — 1232 Grant Ave, SF. The oldest bar in the city, blues nightly in North Beach since 1861. Tip the band.

Eight SF music venues: the Fillmore, Great American Music Hall, Bimbo's, the Chapel, the Warfield, the Independent, Cafe du Nord, and the Saloon. Where do you start?

item.description: San Rafael anchors Marin with a Fourth Street of Puerto Rican comfort food, craft cocktails, and a 1938 art deco movie house. Eight San Rafael stops.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in San Rafael

San Rafael anchors Marin with a Fourth Street of Puerto Rican comfort food, craft cocktails, and a 1938 art deco movie house. Eight San Rafael stops.

Sol Food — 903 Lincoln Ave, San Rafael. The Puerto Rican comfort food spot with a citywide following. Get the pernil.

Il Davide — 901 A St, San Rafael. An upscale Italian room with homemade pasta and arancini. Start with the arancini.

The Tavern on Fourth — 711 4th St, San Rafael. A craft cocktail bar on the main strip. Order a seasonal cocktail.

State Room — 1132 4th St, San Rafael. A downtown bar and gathering spot with a big beer list. Grab a booth.

Rustic Bakery — 1407 4th St, San Rafael. A Marin bakery cafe for flatbreads and pastries. Get a morning pastry.

Whipper Snapper — 1613 4th St, San Rafael. A Caribbean and Latin spot with rum drinks and a patio. Do the jerk chicken.

Ghiringhelli Pizzeria — 1535 4th St, San Rafael. A family pizzeria and sports bar downtown. Split a pie.

Rafael Film Center — 1118 4th St, San Rafael. A restored 1938 art deco theater screening indies. Catch a film.

Eight in San Rafael: Sol Food, Il Davide, the Tavern on Fourth, State Room, Rustic Bakery, Whipper Snapper, Ghiringhelli, and the Rafael. Where do you start?

Ohgane Korean BBQ — 3915 Broadway, Oakland. A Broadway pioneer of Bay Area Korean BBQ since 2006. Get the galbi.

Jong Ga House — 372 Grand Ave, Oakland. A Grand Avenue favorite for banchan and tofu stew since 2000. Order the soondubu.

Pyeong Chang Tofu House — 4701 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A cozy Temescal spot for bubbling soft tofu stew. Get a soondubu pot.

Dan Sung Sa — 2775 Telegraph Ave, Oakland. A dim Korean pub covered in graffiti and old newspapers. Order the pojangmacha snacks.

Um Ma — 1220 9th Ave, SF. An Inner Sunset spot for homestyle Korean and galbi jjim. Get the galbi jjim.

Han Il Kwan — 1802 Balboa St, SF. A Richmond standby for Korean BBQ and stews. Get the bulgogi.

Manna — 845 Irving St, SF. A tiny Inner Sunset counter with a steady line. Get the dolsot bibimbap.

Jang Su Jang — 3561 El Camino Real, Santa Clara. A South Bay BBQ hall with premium cuts. Do a full BBQ spread.

item.content:encoded:

The Bay Area does Indian food from a legendary Berkeley chaat counter to Michelin dining rooms in Palo Alto and Burlingame, among the deepest scenes in the country. Eight Bay Area Indian tables.

Vik's Chaat — 2390 4th St, Berkeley. The legendary chaat house for pani puri and cholle bhature. Get a plate of chaat.

Rooh — 333 Brannan St, SF. Modern Indian near the ballpark with creative small plates. Do the chef's picks.

Besharam — 1275 Minnesota St, SF. A Gujarati spot from a celebrated chef in Dogpatch. Order the thali.

Breads of India — 2448 Sacramento St, Berkeley. A daily changing North Indian menu. Try the daily thali.

Ajanta — 1888 Solano Ave, Berkeley. A regional Indian spot with a rotating monthly menu. Ask the special.

Fitoor — Santana Row, San Jose. A modern Indian restaurant in the former Amber India space on Santana Row, tandoor plates and cocktails. Order the butter chicken.

Ettan — 518 Bryant St, Palo Alto. A Michelin recognized modern Indian downtown. Book the tasting.

Rasa — 209 Park Rd, Burlingame. A Michelin starred South Indian on the Peninsula. Do the tasting.

Eight for Indian: Vik's Chaat, Rooh, Besharam, Breads of India, Ajanta, Fitoor, Ettan, and Rasa. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Sushi

The Bay Area's sushi runs from a downtown omakase counter open since 1987 to a Sausalito landmark by the water, some of the best fish outside Tokyo. Eight Bay Area sushi counters.

Akiko's — 431 Bush St, SF. SF's pioneering omakase since 1987, pristine nigiri downtown. Sit at the bar.

Ju-Ni — 1335 Fulton St, SF. A counter omakase in a converted flat with chefs seat side. Book the counter.

Robin — 620 Gough St, SF. A playful Hayes Valley omakase with no printed menu. Trust the chef.

Sasaki — 2400 Harrison St, SF. A refined Mission omakase from a Kusakabe alum. Reserve ahead.

Kappou Gomi — 5524 Geary Blvd, SF. A Richmond spot for traditional Japanese, no rolls, just craft. Order the seasonal set.

Sushi Ran — 107 Caledonia St, Sausalito. A Marin sushi landmark for nearly forty years. Order the omakase.

Delage — 536 9th St, Oakland. An intimate Oakland Chinatown omakase counter. Book the seating.

Sushi Sam's Edomata — 218 E 3rd Ave, San Mateo. A Peninsula cult favorite for market fresh nigiri. Ask the daily specials.

Eight for sushi: Akiko's, Ju-Ni, Robin, Sasaki, Kappou Gomi, Sushi Ran, Delage, and Sushi Sam's. Where do you start?

item.description: San Francisco's dive bars are living history, from a 1937 Chinatown lounge pouring Chinese mai tais to a Mission beer garden with 40 taps and a Simpsons pi
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Dive Bars

San Francisco's dive bars are living history, from a 1937 Chinatown lounge pouring Chinese mai tais to a Mission beer garden with 40 taps and a Simpsons pinball. Eight SF dive bars.

Zeitgeist — 199 Valencia St, SF. A beer garden dive with a huge backyard and famous bloody marys. Grab a picnic table.

Specs' Twelve Adler Museum Cafe — 12 William Saroyan Pl, SF. A cluttered North Beach classic since 1968. Squeeze in among the bric a brac.

Li Po Lounge — 916 Grant Ave, SF. A cavernous 1937 Chinatown lounge famous for Chinese mai tais. Order a mai tai.

The 500 Club — 500 Guerrero St, SF. A 1953 Mission den under a neon marquee. Post up at the bar.

The Homestead — 2301 Folsom St, SF. A Victorian corner bar with peanut shells on the floor. Shell some peanuts.

Kilowatt — 3160 16th St, SF. A Mission rock dive that birthed the Noise Pop festival. Catch a band.

Aub Zam Zam — 1633 Haight St, SF. A 1940s martini bar with a Persian mural and Sinatra on the box. Order a gin martini.

Bender's — 806 S Van Ness Ave, SF. A grungy Mission dive with tater tots and metal. Get tots and a shot.

Eight SF dive bars: Zeitgeist, Specs', Li Po Lounge, the 500 Club, the Homestead, Kilowatt, Aub Zam Zam, and Bender's. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in Los Altos

Los Altos hides a small town downtown in the middle of Silicon Valley, where a 1970 family Chinese icon and a French bakery share the plazas with venture offices. Eight Los Altos stops.

State of Mind Public House and Pizzeria — 101 Plaza N, Los Altos. A sourdough pizza and craft beer hall on the plaza. Split a sourdough pie.

Voyageur du Temps — 288 1st St, Los Altos. A French bakery and cafe for croissants and quiche. Get a croissant.

Los Altos Grill — 233 3rd St, Los Altos. A polished American grill and bar downtown. Order the burger.

Sumika — 236 Central Plaza, Los Altos. A tiny Japanese grill for charcoal skewers. Get the yakitori set.

Chef Chu's — 1067 N San Antonio Rd, Los Altos. An iconic Chinese restaurant since 1970. Order the lettuce cups.

Linden Tree Books — 170 State St, Los Altos. A longtime children's bookstore on the strip. Pick out a picture book.

Cetrella — 400 Main St, Los Altos. An upscale Mediterranean room downtown. Book dinner.

Los Altos History Museum — 51 S San Antonio Rd, Los Altos. A free local museum beside an old adobe. Walk the orchard story.

Eight in Los Altos: State of Mind, Voyageur du Temps, Los Altos Grill, Sumika, Chef Chu's, Linden Tree Books, Cetrella, and the History Museum. Where do you start?

Bay Area Thai

The Bay Area's Thai food earned a Michelin star near Union Square and runs deep from a Tenderloin institution to Lao and Thai kitchens across the East Bay. Eight Bay Area Thai tables.

Kin Khao — 55 Cyril Magnin St, SF. A Michelin starred Thai kitchen just off Union Square. Get the rabbit curry.

Nari — 1625 Post St, SF. A modern Thai room in Japantown from the Kin Khao chef. Do the tasting.

Lers Ros — 730 Larkin St, SF. A Tenderloin institution with a huge authentic menu. Order the crispy pork.

Farmhouse Kitchen Thai — 710 Florida St, SF. A festive Mission spot for northern Thai and cocktails. Get the khao soi.

Hawker Fare — 680 Valencia St, SF. A rice bowl spot rooted in Isan Lao and Thai flavors. Get a jasmine rice bowl.

Anchalee — 1094 Dwight Way, Berkeley. A Berkeley favorite for fresh, balanced Thai. Order the curry noodles.

Champa Garden — 2102 8th Ave, Oakland. An Oakland spot for Lao and Thai home cooking. Try the nam khao.

Amarin Thai — 156 Castro St, Mountain View. A downtown Mountain View Thai standby. Get the pad see ew.

Eight for Thai: Kin Khao, Nari, Lers Ros, Farmhouse Kitchen, Hawker Fare, Anchalee, Champa Garden, and Amarin. Where do you start?

item.description: When the bars close, San Francisco eats at a 1920s diner shaped like a rail car open till 4am and a Mission taqueria slinging burritos long past midnight.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Late Night Eats

When the bars close, San Francisco eats at a 1920s diner shaped like a rail car open till 4am and a Mission taqueria slinging burritos long past midnight. Eight SF late night eats.

Grubstake — 1525 Pine St, SF. A diner in an old rail car serving burgers and Portuguese plates till the small hours. Get a burger at 2am.

El Farolito — 2779 Mission St, SF. The late night Mission taqueria for a foil wrapped super burrito. Order the al pastor.

Taqueria Cancun — 2288 Mission St, SF. A neon lit taqueria beloved for its late tacos. Get the carne asada.

Golden Boy Pizza — 542 Green St, SF. A North Beach counter slinging square Sicilian slices till late. Grab a clam and garlic square.

Yuet Lee — 1300 Stockton St, SF. A bright green Chinatown seafood spot for late salt and pepper squid. Order the squid.

Bob's Donuts — 1621 Polk St, SF. A 24 hour donut stop for a 3am apple fritter. Get the fritter warm.

Orphan Andy's — 3991 17th St, SF. A round the clock Castro diner with pancakes and shakes. Order a milkshake.

Pearl's Deluxe Burgers — 708 Post St, SF. A late night burger and shake window downtown. Get a Kobe burger.

Eight late night eats: Grubstake, El Farolito, Taqueria Cancun, Golden Boy, Yuet Lee, Bob's Donuts, Orphan Andy's, and Pearl's. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in San Carlos

San Carlos calls itself the City of Good Living, and its Laurel Street packs a Belgian pastrami temple, a Greek taverna, and wood fired pizza into a few Peninsula blocks. Eight San Carlos stops.

PYLOS — 621 Laurel St, San Carlos. A Greek taverna with grilled octopus and saganaki. Order the octopus.

888 Ristorante Italiano — 888 Laurel St, San Carlos. A downtown Italian room with handmade pasta. Split the pasta.

Rouge Wine Bar — 890 Laurel St, San Carlos. A cozy wine bar with boards and by the glass pours. Ask for a flight.

Pazzo — 1179 Laurel St, San Carlos. A Neapolitan pizzeria with wood fired pies and housemade pasta. Get a Margherita.

The Refuge — 963 Laurel St, San Carlos. A cult spot for house cured pastrami and hundreds of Belgian beers. Order the pastrami.

Number5 Kitchen — 720 Laurel St, San Carlos. A modern American bistro on the main strip. Do the tasting plates.

Dumpling and Dough — 1131 Laurel St, San Carlos. A quick spot for soup dumplings and noodles. Get the xiao long bao.

Cafe La Tartine — 1219 Laurel St, San Carlos. A French cafe for crepes and croissants. Grab a crepe.

Eight in San Carlos: PYLOS, 888 Ristorante, Rouge, Pazzo, the Refuge, Number5 Kitchen, Dumpling and Dough, and Cafe La Tartine. Where do you start?

The Bay Area has flipped burgers the same way since 1958 at a San Leandro drive in, and the best patties run from a Berkeley college counter to a Palo Alto soda fountain. Eight Bay Area burgers.

Val's Burgers — 75 Estudillo Ave, San Leandro. A family burger joint griddling since 1958, get the double Papa Burger. Order the Papa.

Super Duper Burgers — 721 Market St, SF. A local chain of griddled burgers and garlic fries. Add the garlic fries.

Causwells — 2346 Chestnut St, SF. A Marina spot with the smashed Americana double. Get the Americana.

WesBurger N More — 2240 Mission St, SF. A Mission smashburger counter with retro sauces. Order the classic.

Barney's Gourmet Hamburgers — 1591 Solano Ave, Berkeley. An East Bay burger institution with chili cheese fries. Get the curly fries.

Nation's Giant Hamburgers — 10630 San Pablo Ave, El Cerrito. A 24 hour Bay Area classic for burgers and pie. Add a slice of pie.

Palo Alto Creamery — 566 Emerson St, Palo Alto. A 1920s soda fountain for burgers and milkshakes. Get a burger and a shake.

Bongo Burger — 2154 Center St, Berkeley. A UC Berkeley burger and Persian joint since 1969. Get the classic burger.

item.content:encoded:

San Francisco has done date night the same way for 30 years at a Nob Hill Italian temple, and the city still sets the mood from a Mission courtyard cinema to a bay view raw bar. Eight SF date night restaurants.

Acquerello — 1722 Sacramento St, SF. A Nob Hill Italian fine dining room for a milestone night. Do the tasting menu.

Gary Danko — 800 N Point St, SF. A polished tasting menu institution near the wharf. Build a plate flight.

Frances — 3870 17th St, SF. A warm Castro bistro with market driven California cooking. Get the bacon beignets.

Zuni Cafe — 1658 Market St, SF. The iconic wood oven room famous for a roast chicken for two. Order the chicken.

Foreign Cinema — 2534 Mission St, SF. A Mission courtyard restaurant screening films on the wall. Book the patio.

Aziza — 5800 Geary Blvd, SF. A Michelin Cal Moroccan room in the Richmond. Get the basteeya.

Octavia — 1701 Octavia St, SF. A refined neighborhood tasting spot in Pacific Heights. Sit at the counter.

Angler — 132 The Embarcadero, SF. A Michelin seafood room with a raw bar and bay view. Book a window at sunset.

Eight for date night: Acquerello, Gary Danko, Frances, Zuni Cafe, Foreign Cinema, Aziza, Octavia, and Angler. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in Menlo Park

Menlo Park hides an old school downtown at the edge of Silicon Valley, where a legendary independent bookstore and its next door cafe have anchored the block for generations. Eight Menlo Park stops.

Camper — 898 Santa Cruz Ave, Menlo Park. A market driven Californian room on the main strip. Do the tasting plates.

Porta Blu — 200 Independence Dr, Menlo Park. A polished New American dining room at Hotel Nia, seasonal plates and craft cocktails. Order the seasonal plates.

Bistro Vida — 641 Santa Cruz Ave, Menlo Park. A cozy French bistro with sidewalk seating. Get the steak frites.

Ann's Coffee Shop — 796 Santa Cruz Ave, Menlo Park. A classic old school diner for breakfast. Order the pancakes.

Kepler's Books — 1010 El Camino Real, Menlo Park. A legendary independent bookstore since 1955. Catch an author talk.

Cafe Borrone — 1010 El Camino Real, Menlo Park. The bustling cafe next to Kepler's for coffee and people watching. Grab a patio table.

Flea Street — 3607 Alameda de las Pulgas, Menlo Park. A farm to table pioneer running for decades. Book dinner.

Naomi Sushi — 1328 El Camino Real, Menlo Park. A longtime neighborhood sushi bar. Sit at the bar.

Eight in Menlo Park: Camper, Porta Blu, Bistro Vida, Ann's Coffee Shop, Kepler's Books, Cafe Borrone, Flea Street, and Naomi Sushi. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Donuts

The Bay Area's donut game runs from a 24 hour Polk Street counter open since 1960 to a Berkeley shop that put mochi donuts on the map. Eight Bay Area donut shops.

Bob's Donuts — 1621 Polk St, SF. A 24 hour SF counter since 1960, home of a giant apple fritter. Get the fritter warm.

Dynamo Donut — 2760 24th St, SF. A Mission shop of small batch flavors like maple bacon apple. Try the maple bacon.

Johnny Doughnuts — 1617 4th St, San Rafael. A Marin favorite of organic doughnuts and the cronut style Johnnut. Get a Johnnut.

Donut Savant — 6037 San Pablo Ave, Oakland. An Oakland shop of square cronuts and tiny bites. Grab a box of minis.

Colonial Donuts — 3318 Lakeshore Ave, Oakland. A 24 hour Lakeshore classic since the 1980s. Get a buttermilk bar at 2am.

King Pin Donuts — 2521 Durant Ave, Berkeley. A 24 hour Berkeley institution since 1939 for classic raised and cake donuts by the dozen. Order a dozen warm.

Third Culture Bakery — 2701 Eighth St, Berkeley. The Berkeley shop that popularized the mochi muffin and mochi donut. Get a mochi donut.

Psycho Donuts — 288 S 2nd St, San Jose. A wacky South Bay shop of over the top creations. Get something ridiculous.

item.content:encoded:
San Francisco SF's Dessert Shops

San Francisco has a serious sweet tooth, from a bourbon and corn flake ice cream in the Mission to a chocolate factory that roasts its own beans on Valencia Street. Eight SF dessert shops.

Bi-Rite Creamery — 3692 18th St, SF. The Mission ice cream counter with a line around the block for salted caramel. Get the salted caramel.

Humphry Slocombe — 2790A Harrison St, SF. The home of Secret Breakfast, bourbon ice cream with corn flakes. Order Secret Breakfast.

Craftsman and Wolves — 746 Valencia St, SF. A modern patisserie famous for the Rebel Within savory muffin. Get the Rebel Within.

Dandelion Chocolate — 740 Valencia St, SF. A bean to bar chocolate factory and cafe with s'mores. Do the hot chocolate flight.

Miette — 1 Ferry Building, SF. A dainty pastel patisserie of cakes and macarons. Take home a gingerbread cake.

Garden Creamery — 3566 20th St, SF. A Hawaiian inspired ice cream shop with mochi and vegan scoops. Try the ube.

Anthony's Cookies — 1417 Valencia St, SF. A tiny shop for warm, chewy, chocolate chip cookies. Get them by the box.

Schubert's Bakery — 521 Clement St, SF. A Richmond German bakery making cakes since 1911. Get a slice of Princess cake.

item.title: San Francisco A Day in Mill Valley
item.description: Mill Valley is the Bay Area's woodsy hideaway at the foot of Mount Tam, where a 1929 train depot turned bookstore cafe anchors a downtown ringed by redwood
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in Mill Valley

Mill Valley is the Bay Area's woodsy hideaway at the foot of Mount Tam, where a 1929 train depot turned bookstore cafe anchors a downtown ringed by redwoods. Eight Mill Valley stops.

Depot Cafe and Bookstore — 87 Throckmorton Ave, Mill Valley. A 1929 rail depot turned cafe and bookstore on the plaza. Read on the patio.

La Ginestra — 127 Throckmorton Ave, Mill Valley. A family Italian spot serving the town since 1964. Get the ravioli.

Piazza D'Angelo — 22 Miller Ave, Mill Valley. A bustling Italian trattoria and bar downtown. Sit on the patio.

Equator Coffees — 2 Miller Ave, Mill Valley. A corner cafe from a certified sustainable roaster. Order a cortado.

Watershed — 129 Miller Ave, Mill Valley. A California kitchen in the old Mill Valley lumberyard. Get a wood fired dish.

Sweetwater Music Hall — 19 Corte Madera Ave, Mill Valley. A legendary small music hall with big surprise guests. Catch a late show.

Mill Valley Market — 12 Corte Madera Ave, Mill Valley. A 1929 family grocery with a great deli counter. Build a picnic.

Old Mill Park — Throckmorton Ave, Mill Valley. A redwood park with a creek and the town's old sawmill. Walk under the redwoods.

Eight in Mill Valley: the Depot, La Ginestra, Piazza D'Angelo, Equator Coffees, Watershed, Sweetwater Music Hall, Mill Valley Market, and Old Mill Park. Where do you start?

item.title: SF Bay Area Farmers Markets
item.description: The SF Bay Area shops for groceries at the Ferry Building's showcase market and the oldest farmers market in the state, running under a freeway in San Fran
item.content:encoded:
SF Bay Area Farmers Markets

The SF Bay Area shops for groceries at the Ferry Building's showcase market and the oldest farmers market in the state, running under a freeway in San Francisco since 1943. Eight SF Bay Area farmers markets.

Ferry Plaza Farmers Market — 1 Ferry Building, SF. The famous Saturday market of top farms and chefs on the waterfront. Go early for the peaches.

Alemany Farmers Market — 100 Alemany Blvd, SF. The people's market, the oldest in the state since 1943. Bring cash and a cart.

Grand Lake Farmers Market — 746 Grand Ave, Oakland. A big Saturday market by Lake Merritt with prepared food galore. Get dim sum to walk with.

Old Oakland Farmers Market — 9th St, Oakland. A Friday market in the historic Victorian blocks. Shop then brunch nearby.

Berkeley Farmers Market — Center St, Berkeley. A pioneering organic market downtown on Saturdays. Fill a bag with greens.

Marin Civic Center Farmers Market — 3501 Civic Center Dr, San Rafael. One of the biggest weekly markets in the state, Sundays and Thursdays. Come hungry.

Mountain View Farmers Market — 600 W Evelyn Ave, Mountain View. A big Sunday market at the Caltrain lot with 70 growers. Graze the stalls.

Temescal Farmers Market — 5300 Claremont Ave, Oakland. A lively Sunday market in the DMV lot with hot food. Grab breakfast there.

Eight markets: Ferry Plaza, Alemany, Grand Lake, Old Oakland, Berkeley, Marin Civic Center, Mountain View, and Temescal. Where do you start?

item.title: Bay Area Day Trips You Sent Us
item.description: Every Bay Area day trip post fills with your own detours, so this whole list is the stops readers told us we missed, from the Sonoma coast to a Lodi zinfan
item.content:encoded:
Bay Area Day Trips You Sent Us

Every Bay Area day trip post fills with your own detours, so this whole list is the stops readers told us we missed, from the Sonoma coast to a Lodi zinfandel. Eight Bay Area day trips.

River's End — 11048 Highway 1, Jenner. A bluff top restaurant over the mouth of the Russian River in Jenner. Book lunch for the view. A @artsyyvonne add.

Jettywave Distillery — 155 Broadway, Half Moon Bay. A newer Half Moon Bay distillery with outdoor seating and good vibes. Do a spirits tasting. A @waynemo66 add.

Rosicrucian Egyptian Museum — 1660 Park Ave, San Jose. The largest collection of Egyptian artifacts on the West Coast, near the Rose Garden. See the mummies. A @coopertown104 add.

Radke Martinez Regional Shoreline — 1 Ferry St, Martinez. A flat waterfront walk on the Carquinez Strait readers said not to miss. Walk the marsh boardwalk. A @lady_chapin add.

Macchia Wines — 7099 E Peltier Rd, Acampo. A family Lodi winery readers praise for its bold reds. Taste the Zinfandels. A @salcidoterry add.

The Restaurant at North Block — 6757 Washington St, Yountville. A Yountville hotel restaurant with a fantastic bar and wine list. Sit at the bar. A @brennaleeroth add.

Grassy Bar Oyster Company — 1215 Embarcadero Rd, Morro Bay. A no frills Morro Bay shop selling fresh oysters on the half shell. Slurp a dozen by the water. A @asianhalfpint add.

Tierra Luna Cellars — Acampo. A Lodi area winery from former astronaut Jose Hernandez. Pour the astronaut's red. A @salcidoterry add.

Eight Bay Area day trips: River's End, Jettywave, the Rosicrucian, the Martinez Shoreline, Macchia, North Block, Grassy Bar, and Tierra Luna. Which one first?

item.content:encoded:
San Francisco A Day in Benicia

Benicia is the Bay Area's overlooked waterfront town, a former state capital where First Street runs straight down to the Carquinez Strait. Eight Benicia stops.

Sailor Jack's — 123 First St, Benicia. A waterfront seafood spot at the bottom of First Street. Get a window table.

Drift Benicia — 366 First St, Benicia. A downtown pizza and coffee stop. Grab a slice and an espresso.

Lucca Bar and Grill — 439 First St, Benicia. A gastropub with a beer garden and live music. Sit in the garden.

Rellik Tavern — 726 First St, Benicia. A cozy tavern in a historic downtown building. Order a cocktail.

One House Bakery — 918 First St, Benicia. A wildly popular bakery on upper First Street. Get there before the pastries sell out.

Benicia Capitol State Historic Park — 115 West G St, Benicia. The only surviving pre Sacramento state capitol. Tour the 1852 chamber.

Benicia Historical Museum — 2060 Camel Rd, Benicia. A museum in 1850s sandstone buildings in the old Arsenal. Walk the Arsenal grounds.

Matthew Turner Shipyard Park — 1001 West 12th St, Benicia. A waterfront park honoring the busiest shipbuilder in North America. Watch the boats.

Eight in Benicia: Sailor Jack's, Drift, Lucca, Rellik Tavern, One House Bakery, the Capitol, the Historical Museum, and Shipyard Park. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:

Provisions — 300 Virginia St, Vallejo. A downtown restaurant and community gathering spot. Come for a weekend dinner.

Alibi Bookshop — Georgia St, Vallejo. An indie bookshop anchoring the arts walk. Browse the local shelf.

Empress Theatre — 330 Virginia St, Vallejo. A restored historic theater for live music and film. Catch a show.

Coal Shed Brewery — Mare Island, Vallejo. A brewery in a former naval munitions shed with strait views. Drink a beer by the water.

Mare Island Brewing Ferry Taproom — Vallejo waterfront. The ferry terminal taproom pouring local craft beer. Grab a beer before the ferry.

Vallejo Naval and Historical Museum — Marin St, Vallejo. A museum of the city's Navy and Mare Island history. Dig into the shipyard past.

Vallejo Ferry — Mare Island Way, Vallejo. The fast ferry to San Francisco from the waterfront. Ride it across the bay.

item.content:encoded:

Abbott Square Market — 725 Front St, Santa Cruz. A food hall and plaza with live music behind the museum. Graze the stalls.

item.content:encoded:

Capitola is the Bay Area's pastel beach village, among the oldest seaside resort towns on the coast, where a wharf and a lagoon meet a row of candy colored cottages. Eight Capitola Village stops.

Zelda's on the Beach — Esplanade, Capitola. A family beachfront spot since 1978 for a patio breakfast. Eat right on the sand.

Shadowbrook — 1750 Wharf Rd, Capitola. A hillside special occasion restaurant you reach by cable car since 1947. Ride the cable car down.

Mr Toots Coffeehouse — Esplanade, Capitola. A second floor espresso bar with a village view. Take a coffee to the balcony.

Margaritaville — Esplanade, Capitola. A beachfront Mexican bar and grill. Order a margarita on the deck.

Capitola Wharf — Capitola. The historic pier reaching out over the bay. Walk out over the water.

item.content:encoded:

Nevada City is the Bay Area's favorite Gold Rush day trip, a perfectly preserved Victorian downtown of gaslit brick, an 1865 theater, and a brewery in an old bakery. Eight Nevada City stops.

Nevada Theatre — 401 Broad St, Nevada City. A California theater running since 1865, among the state's oldest. Catch a show or a film.

Three Forks Bakery and Brewing — 211 Commercial St, Nevada City. A bakery and brewery with wood fired pizza and house beer. Get a pizza and a pint.

Crazy Horse Saloon and Grill — 230 Commercial St, Nevada City. A downtown saloon with live music and comfort food. Stay for the band.

Golden Era — 309 Broad St, Nevada City. A historic saloon reborn as a cocktail and jazz lounge. Order a craft cocktail.

Off Broadstreet — 305 Commercial St, Nevada City. A cabaret theater in the heart of downtown. Catch a variety show.

Outside Inn — 575 E Broad St, Nevada City. A quirky mid century motor lodge for the night. Book a themed room.

Broad Street — Nevada City. The gaslit main drag of shops and Victorians. Stroll the historic blocks.

Deer Creek Tribute Trail — Nevada City. A creekside trail right off downtown. Walk down to the creek.

Eight in Nevada City: the Nevada Theatre, Three Forks, the Crazy Horse, Golden Era, Off Broadstreet, the Outside Inn, Broad Street, and Deer Creek. Where do you start?

item.content:encoded:

Bodega Bay is the Bay Area's closest slice of the Sonoma Coast, a fishing harbor of fresh crab shacks, a windswept headland, and the church from Hitchcock's The Birds. Eight Bodega Bay stops.

Spud Point Crab Company — 1910 Westshore Rd, Bodega Bay. An old style crab shack for chowder and crab sandwiches. Get the crab sandwich.

The Tides Wharf — 835 Highway 1, Bodega Bay. A harborside seafood restaurant and fish market. Watch the boats over lunch.

Fishetarian Fish Market — 599 Highway 1, Bodega Bay. A market for fish and chips and clam chowder. Order the fish and chips.

Gourmet Au Bay — 1412 Bay Flat Rd, Bodega Bay. A wood oven and wine bar over the water. Sip a glass on the deck.

Bodega Head — Bodega Bay. A windswept headland for whale watching and bluff trails. Hike the bluff loop.

Doran Beach — 201 Doran Beach Rd, Bodega Bay. A two mile sand spit for beachcombing and kites. Walk the spit.

St Teresa of Avila Church — Bodega. The white steepled church made famous by The Birds. Photograph the steeple.

Bodega Bay harbor — Bodega Bay. The working fishing harbor of boats and pelicans. Watch the fleet come in.

item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Record Stores

Amoeba on Haight fills a former bowling alley, and the old bowling marquee still sits up on the roof. Everybody heads there. The real crate digging in San Francisco hides in the smaller shops most people walk right past. Eight record stores worth the trip.

Amoeba Music — 1855 Haight St, San Francisco. The cavernous main room gets the tourists, but regulars make for the used bins and the bargain vinyl along the walls, and the free in store shows pull real crowds. Go on a weekday morning before the racks get picked over. @amoebasf

Rooky Ricardo's Records — 419 Haight St, San Francisco. Soul, funk, and doo wop 45s stacked deep, with a counter where they will spin one for you before you commit. Bring cash and give yourself a couple hours. @rooky_ricardos_records

Groove Merchant Records — 687 Haight St, San Francisco. A tiny Lower Haight room packed with rare soul, funk, and jazz that DJs fly in for, written up among the world's best record shops. Squeeze in and dig. @groovemerchantsf

Vinyl Dreams — 593 Haight St, San Francisco. The house, techno, and disco specialist, run by a former Amoeba electronic buyer, with listening stations so you can test imports before buying. If you chase 12 inch dance records, start here. @vinyldreamssf

Grooves — 1797 Market St, San Francisco. A vinyl only holdout near the Castro, heavy on oddball soundtracks, spoken word, and pop obscurities you did not know you needed. Great for the record you cannot find anywhere else. @groovesvinyl

Stranded Records — 1055 Valencia St, San Francisco. The record store arm of a reissue label, so the walls lean avant garde, punk, jazz, and experimental, tightly chosen, not sprawling. Come for the stuff the big shops skip. @strandedrecords

Originals Vinyl — 701 Fillmore St, San Francisco. A small family run used shop that also cleans and de warps records on an ultrasonic machine, with new arrivals daily. Bring that warped LP that has been sitting in your attic. @originalsvinyl

101 Music — 1414 Grant Ave, San Francisco. The last record shop in North Beach, actually two crammed storefronts, one for records and one for vintage instruments and stereo gear. Squeeze past the stacks and you will find something.

Eight for the record hunt: Amoeba, Rooky Ricardo's, Groove Merchant, Vinyl Dreams, Grooves, Stranded, Originals Vinyl, and 101 Music. Which bin do you lose track of time in?

item.title: San Francisco Vintage and Thrift Shops
item.description: Wasteland on Haight sells vintage out of a 1911 theater, an ornate Art Nouveau facade now painted fire engine red you can spot a block away. San Francisco
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco Vintage and Thrift Shops

Wasteland on Haight sells vintage out of a 1911 theater, an ornate Art Nouveau facade now painted fire engine red you can spot a block away. San Francisco keeps its best secondhand on a handful of streets, not scattered across town. Eight vintage and thrift stops worth a Saturday.

Wasteland — 1660 Haight St, San Francisco. Behind that red facade is a huge floor of vintage denim, leather, and designer resale, and they buy off the street if you bring a bag to sell. Go early for the good size runs. @shopwasteland

Buffalo Exchange — 1555 Haight St, San Francisco. The dependable buy sell trade up the same block, well sorted and cheaper than the boutiques, paying cash or store credit on the spot. Bring a bag to sell and walk out with something new. @buffaloexchange

Relic Vintage — 1475 Haight St, San Francisco. This one leans older and dressier, real 1940s to 1960s pieces, hats, and costume jewelry, not 90s castoffs. The place to find something for a themed party that actually looks the part. @relicvintage

Crossroads Trading — 1901 Fillmore St, San Francisco. Over on Fillmore, this leans current and on trend resale, so it is the spot for near new brands at a fraction of retail. Check the clearance rack in the back first. @crossroadstrading

Relove — 1815 Polk St, San Francisco. A Black owned resale boutique on Polk with a tight, well priced mix of vintage and designer, more boutique than warehouse dig. Easy in and out when you want quality over quantity. @shoprelove

No Shop — 389 Valencia St, San Francisco. Kicks off the Valencia vintage stretch with cheap band tees, jewelry, and eclectic racks that reward a slow flip. Come for a $25 tee, stay for the odd jacket you did not plan on. @no_shop

Community Thrift Store — 623 Valencia St, San Francisco. A big nonprofit thrift where donations get credited to a local charity the giver names, so your bargain hunt quietly funds the neighborhood. Hit the books and housewares, not just the clothes. @communitythriftsf

Valencia Street Vintage — 714 Valencia St, San Francisco. A small, well edited shop with a killer $15 rack and rotating local art on the walls. A good last stop on a Valencia crawl when your arms are already full. @valenciastreetvintage

Eight for a vintage crawl: Wasteland, Buffalo Exchange, Relic Vintage, Crossroads Trading, Relove, No Shop, Community Thrift, and Valencia Street Vintage. Haight, Fillmore, or Valencia, which block do you start on?
